title: Farrales mango: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Farrales mango: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Farrales mango is a Carabao mango variety from Perla A. Farrales. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Farrales mango is a Carabao mango variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2020 as NSIC 2020 Mn 17. Perla A. Farrales bred it. Its record notes a yield of about 200 kg.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Farrales mango is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [mango variety finder](/crop-varieties/mango), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of about 200 kg.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Farrales was over 30 years old and about 12 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of about 200 kg. It bears twice a year, with fruit in January February and July August. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit mango fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Mango cecid fly (kurikong)](/pests/mango-cecid-fly), [Mango leafhopper](/pests/mango-leafhopper), [Mango pulp weevil](/pests/mango-pulp-weevil), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Farrales weighs about 222.68 grams, and its shape is ellipsoid. The flesh is orange and intermediate. Its sweetness measured 16.62 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 69.58 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as January February and July August, bearing semi annual.
Where and when to plant Farrales mango

The Carabao mango is the one the market wants, and the registered strains are its best trees, picked for size, sweetness and steady bearing. Buy grafted seedlings from a BPI accredited nursery so you get the strain you paid for. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.
